subject: ‘It’s a buyers’ market’: First home buyers snap up $1.8m inner-city home
posts:
Sydney property resilience meets high interest rates as first home buyers secure an Alexandria townhouse for $1.8m.
Evidence: Auction results, agent quotes, RBA rate hikes
#Aletheia #RealEstate 🌐

Agents claim it's a buyers' market where strong demand persists despite rising mortgage costs and bidder dropouts.
Stated Judgement: (+0.50, +0.50) — Greater Good

Routine property transactions continue despite rate hikes, reflecting localized demand rather than systemic collapse.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.40, +0.00) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — Fall from Grace.
Standard market activity proceeds under normal economic friction without systemic deception.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.1, z: 0)
First home buyers successfully purchased a tri-level Alexandria home at auction amid 671 scheduled Sydney auctions this week.
Withdrawing bidders cited financing issues following the Reserve Bank's fifth interest rate hike, yet demand held firm.

The Bright Side:
High buyer resilience shows underlying market liquidity despite aggressive monetary tightening.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing marketing spin ('buyers' market') with structural economic shifts. This is an ordinary commercial transaction.

Social Physics Analysis:
Sellers and agents frame high prices as a buyer advantage to maintain transaction momentum, managing market psychology without predatory extraction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall from Grace.
Modal Dynamics: can be -> can be via Destructive Geodesic.
Standard commercial exchange remains anchored in local reality.

The Unavoidable Truth: Local real estate auctions reflect individual financial capacity rather than macroeconomic collapse.

The Unavoidable Lie: Marketing spin claiming a high-priced auction is purely a buyers' paradise.

Alethekanon:
Ordinary market friction is often dressed in optimistic real estate jargon, yet concrete bids decide reality.

Awwthekanon:
Buying a first home is a monumental milestone, especially amid rising financial pressures. May this new chapter bring true security and peace.

Brothekanon:
Rates are climbing and bidders are dropping out, but people are still dropping nearly two million bucks on townhouses. Wild market.

Spirithekanon:
"Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right." Proverbs 16:8 PASS
True wealth lies in honest living rather than speculative property bubbles.

‘It’s a buyers’ market’: First home buyers snap up $1.8m inner-city home

Two expected bidders pulled out before auction, leaving two others to compete for the three-bedroom house. It didn’t stop the final price exceeding the reserve.

A first home buyer couple from the lower north shore won the keys to a tri-level home in Alexandria, paying $1,803,000 under the hammer on Saturday.

Bidding for 28 Gerard Street opened at $1.55 million, $50,000 below the guide of $1.6 million. Auctioneer Damien Cooley then took bids of $10,000 in quick succession until it hit $1.8 million, when they dropped back to three bids of $1000 and the hammer fell.

The three-bedroom property had a reserve of $1.75 million.

There is no legal requirement for a vendor’s reserve to be in line with their property’s price guide.

Brad Gillespie, sales agent for The Agency, said he was expecting four bidders to attend based on requested contract amendments, but two groups pulled out at the last minute.

“One said something had come up but the other said it was an issue with finances,” he said.

The Reserve Bank this week raised interest rates for a fifth time this year to 4.85 per cent.

Gillespie said confident bidding and a result above the reserve was indicative of growing confidence at this end of the market.

“We all know it’s a buyers’ market and vendors know that as well,” he said. “If it’s a property they really like, [buyers] should be going for it.”

The vendors are looking to upsize.

The property was one of 671 scheduled to go to auction in Sydney this week.

In Randwick, a family with plans to “flip” the property won the keys to the apartment with a balcony and parking space, paying $812,000 at auction.

The two-bedroom unit at 1D/12 Bligh Place was a mortgagee in possession sale following a deceased estate.

Bidding for the property opened at $650,000, followed by a $50,000 bid. Increments then fell back to bids of $10,000 until it reached $800,000, when it dropped back to several bids of $1000 and the property sold. It had a guide of $750,000 and a reserve of $725,000.

Seven parties registered to bid, with four raising their paddles.
